messages.content: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: Writebook shows a live "being edited" indicator in a page's editor: while one
person saves, everyone else with the page open sees who is editing. But a
collaborator removed from the book keeps receiving those pushes: an editor
left open while they still had access keeps showing who is editing — presence
payloads, editor names included, for a page they can no longer edit. The
payload must not go out on a channel a removed collaborator can still be
listening on.

Fix it without breaking the indicator.

# Agent Guidelines

## Testing Conventions

### Use Existing Fixtures
Prefer using existing fixtures over creating new records in tests. For example, use `leaves(:welcome_page)` instead of `books(:handbook).press Page.new(body: "..."), title: "..."`.

### URL Helpers in Tests
Use `_path` helpers instead of `_url` helpers in controller/integration tests unless you need to test across different hosts or explicitly need the full URL.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
get book_slug_path(books(:handbook))
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
get book_slug_url(books(:handbook))
```

### Response Body Assertions
Use `assert_in_body` and `assert_not_in_body` to check if text is present or absent in the response body without DOM manipulation.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
assert_in_body "Expected content"
assert_not_in_body "Unexpected content"
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
assert_includes response.body, "Expected content"
assert_not_includes response.body, "Unexpected content"
```

## Controller Conventions

### Simplified respond_to Blocks
When using `respond_to` with default rendering, omit the `{ render }` block as it's implied.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html
    format.md
  end
end
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html { render }
    format.md { render }
  end
end
```

# Agent Guidelines

## Testing Conventions

### Use Existing Fixtures
Prefer using existing fixtures over creating new records in tests. For example, use `leaves(:welcome_page)` instead of `books(:handbook).press Page.new(body: "..."), title: "..."`.

### URL Helpers in Tests
Use `_path` helpers instead of `_url` helpers in controller/integration tests unless you need to test across different hosts or explicitly need the full URL.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
get book_slug_path(books(:handbook))
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
get book_slug_url(books(:handbook))
```

### Response Body Assertions
Use `assert_in_body` and `assert_not_in_body` to check if text is present or absent in the response body without DOM manipulation.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
assert_in_body "Expected content"
assert_not_in_body "Unexpected content"
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
assert_includes response.body, "Expected content"
assert_not_includes response.body, "Unexpected content"
```

## Controller Conventions

### Simplified respond_to Blocks
When using `respond_to` with default rendering, omit the `{ render }` block as it's implied.

**Preferred:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html
    format.md
  end
end
```

**Avoid:**
```ruby
def show
  respond_to do |format|
    format.html { render }
    format.md { render }
  end
end
```

module Book::Accessable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy
    scope :with_everyone_access, -> { where(everyone_access: true) }
  end

  class_methods do
    def accessable_or_published(user: Current.user)
      if user.present?
        accessable_or_published_books
      else
        published
      end
    end

    def accessable_or_published_books(user: Current.user)
      user.books.or(published).distinct
    end
  end

  def accessable?(user: Current.user)
    accesses.exists?(user: user)
  end

  def editable?(user: Current.user)
    access_for(user: user)&.editor? || user&.administrator?
  end

  def access_for(user: Current.user)
    accesses.find_by(user: user)
  end

  def update_access(editors:, readers:)
    editors = Set.new(editors)
    readers = Set.new(everyone_access? ? User.active.ids : readers)

    all = editors + readers
    all_accesses = all.collect { |user_id|
      { user_id: user_id, level: editors.include?(user_id) ? :editor : :reader }
    }

    accesses.upsert_all(all_accesses, unique_by: [ :book_id, :user_id ])
    accesses.where.not(user_id: all).delete_all
  end
end

class User < ApplicationRecord
  include Role, Transferable

  has_many :sessions, dependent: :destroy
  has_secure_password validations: false

  has_many :accesses, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :books, through: :accesses
  has_many :leaves, through: :books

  after_create :grant_access_to_everyone_books

  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }
  scope :ordered, -> { order(:name) }

  def current?
    self == Current.user
  end

  def deactivate
    transaction do
      sessions.delete_all
      update! active: false, email_address: deactived_email_address
    end
  end

  private
    def deactived_email_address
      email_address&.gsub(/@/, "-deactivated-#{SecureRandom.uuid}@")
    end

    def grant_access_to_everyone_books
      all_accesses = Book.with_everyone_access.ids.collect { |id| { book_id: id, level: :reader } }
      accesses.insert_all(all_accesses)
    end
end

    before_action :set_book

# Stream names are how we identify which updates should go to which users. All streams run over the same
# <tt>Turbo::StreamsChannel</tt>, but each with their own subscription. Since stream names are exposed directly to the user
# via the HTML stream subscription tags, we need to ensure that the name isn't tampered with, so the names are signed
# upon generation and verified upon receipt. All verification happens through the <tt>Turbo.signed_stream_verifier</tt>.
module Turbo::Streams::StreamName
  # Used by <tt>Turbo::StreamsChannel</tt> to verify a signed stream name.
  def verified_stream_name(signed_stream_name)
    Turbo.signed_stream_verifier.verified signed_stream_name
  end

  # Used by <tt>Turbo::StreamsHelper#turbo_stream_from(*streamables)</tt> to generate a signed stream name.
  def signed_stream_name(streamables)
    Turbo.signed_stream_verifier.generate stream_name_from(streamables)
  end

  module ClassMethods
    # Can be used by custom turbo stream channels to obtain signed stream name from <tt>params</tt>
    def verified_stream_name_from_params
      self.class.verified_stream_name(params[:signed_stream_name])
    end
  end

  private
    def stream_name_from(streamables)
      if streamables.is_a?(Array)
        streamables.map  { |streamable| stream_name_from(streamable) }.join(":")
      else
        streamables.then { |streamable| streamable.try(:to_gid_param) || streamable.to_param }
      end
    end

module Turbo::Streams::Broadcasts
  include Turbo::Streams::ActionHelper

  def broadcast_remove_to(*streamables, **opts)

  end

  end

  def broadcast_append_to(*streamables, **opts)

  end

  def broadcast_prepend_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action: :prepend, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_refresh_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_stream_to(*streamables, content: turbo_stream_refresh_tag)
  end

  def broadcast_action_to(*streamables, action:, target: nil, targets: nil, attributes: {}, **rendering)
    broadcast_stream_to(*streamables, content: turbo_stream_action_tag(

    )
  end

  def broadcast_replace_later_to(*streamables, **opts)

  end

  def broadcast_update_later_to(*streamables, **opts)

  end

  def broadcast_before_later_to(*streamables, **opts)

  end

  def broadcast_after_later_to(*streamables, **opts)

  end

  def broadcast_append_later_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_later_to(*streamables, action: :append, **opts)
  end

  def broadcast_prepend_later_to(*streamables, **opts)
    broadcast_action_later_to(*streamables, action: :prepend, **opts)
  end

    refresh_debouncer_for(*streamables, request_id: request_id).debounce do

    end

    streamables.flatten!
    streamables.compact_blank!

      target = convert_to_turbo_stream_dom_id(target)
      targets = convert_to_turbo_stream_dom_id(targets, include_selector: true)
      Turbo::Streams::ActionBroadcastJob.perform_later \
        stream_name_from(streamables), action: action, target: target, targets: targets, attributes: attributes, **rendering
    end

  end

    Turbo::Streams::BroadcastJob.perform_later stream_name_from(streamables), **rendering
  end

  def broadcast_stream_to(*streamables, content:)
    streamables.flatten!
    streamables.compact_blank!

    if streamables.present?
      ActionCable.server.broadcast stream_name_from(streamables), content
    end

    Turbo::ThreadDebouncer.for("turbo-refresh-debouncer-#{stream_name_from(streamables.including(request_id))}")

      render  = rendering.delete(:render)

      if render == false
        nil
      else
        content || html || (render_format(:html, **rendering) if rendering.present?)
      end
    end
end

# Stream names are how we identify which updates should go to which users. All streams run over the same
# <tt>Turbo::StreamsChannel</tt>, but each with their own subscription. Since stream names are exposed directly to the user
# via the HTML stream subscription tags, we need to ensure that the name isn't tampered with, so the names are signed
# upon generation and verified upon receipt. All verification happens through the <tt>Turbo.signed_stream_verifier</tt>.
module Turbo::Streams::StreamName
  # Used by <tt>Turbo::StreamsChannel</tt> to verify a signed stream name.
  def verified_stream_name(signed_stream_name)
    Turbo.signed_stream_verifier.verified signed_stream_name
  end

  # Used by <tt>Turbo::StreamsHelper#turbo_stream_from(*streamables)</tt> to generate a signed stream name.
  def signed_stream_name(streamables)
    Turbo.signed_stream_verifier.generate stream_name_from(streamables)
  end

  module ClassMethods
    # Can be used by custom turbo stream channels to obtain signed stream name from <tt>params</tt>
    def verified_stream_name_from_params
      self.class.verified_stream_name(params[:signed_stream_name])
    end
  end

  private
    def stream_name_from(streamables)
      if streamables.is_a?(Array)
        streamables.map  { |streamable| stream_name_from(streamable) }.join(":")
      else
        streamables.then { |streamable| streamable.try(:to_gid_param) || streamable.to_param }
      end
    end
end

**Analyzing the "Being Edited" Indicator Issue**

Okay, let's break this down. The core problem is that a user who has been removed from a book *shouldn't* keep receiving "being edited" updates for pages they no longer have access to. The current implementation relies on ActionCable and Turbo Streams, which subscribe users to channels. The key is to prevent broadcasts from going to channels a removed user can still be listening to.

I've got the setup in mind: In `app/views/leaves/_being_edited_indicator.html.erb` we're using `turbo_stream_from leaf, :being_edited`, and the controller is broadcasting with `Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_render_later_to @leaf, :being_edited`. The problem is that once a user is *subscribed* to that stream, they stay subscribed even if their access is revoked. This is the crux! The `subscribed` method doesn't re-check access; it just verifies the signature, which remains valid.

The central question is how to make sure the right people *hear* the broadcast. So, how do we prevent this leaking of presence payloads? Let's consider a few options:

1.  **Per-User or Per-Access Streams:** A per-user stream could be defined using something like `[leaf, :being_edited, Current.user]` so a stream is created for *each* user on the `leaf`. When a user loses access, you stop broadcasting to their stream. This feels the most direct, but we need to verify we can easily identify the correct stream name, especially as User IDs are only accessible once the user has *subscribed* to ActionCable.
2.  **Disconnecting/Closing ActionCable:** In theory, disconnecting the ActionCable connection would prevent the user from receiving updates. However, it seems like an aggressive approach to just close connections since users could re-subscribe if they still have access, or they could disconnect/reconnect too often.
3.  **Unsubscribing / Rotating Stream:** This is another solution, but may be more work to keep in sync, as we'd need to keep streams updated.
4.  **Custom Channel with User-Specific Stream + Server-Side Disconnect:** With a custom channel we could enforce logic on the backend to enforce disconnects, however, a user can still be listening.

Now, let's explore in detail the **per-user stream** idea. What are the *precise* steps?
*   A user opens a page editor, and the view includes something like `turbo_stream_from leaf, :being_edited, Current.user`. The channel will then subscribe them to a unique stream, for example: `leaf:1:being_edited:user:A`.
*   When *another* user edits, the broadcast only goes to the streams for active editors. We *only* broadcast to the streams for the current editors to prevent users who have lost access to the payload.
*   The key is: when a user's access *changes*, their stream needs to be stopped / cleaned up. Now, we need to make sure the "clean-up" is robust.

Let's carefully consider this access update process: the `Book#update_access` method updates access records by using `upsert_all` and `delete_all`. Critically, these methods *don't* trigger ActiveRecord callbacks. This means we'll need a mechanism to explicitly handle stream management during access updates. Also, administrators can bypass access checks, so we need to account for them.

Now, let's double-check how access is handled in the UI and tests. This is the path forward!

messages.thinking:
**Analyzing the Writebook "Being Edited" Indicator Issue**

Okay, here's the situation. We've got a system where a live "being edited" indicator in Writebook is powered by ActionCable and Turbo Streams. The problem arises when a collaborator is removed from a book but still has an open editor tab. They continue to receive presence payloads, including editor names, for a page they can no longer edit. This shouldn't happen, and the goal is to fix this without breaking the existing indicator functionality.

1.  **The Root Cause**: The core issue stems from how ActionCable subscriptions and broadcasts are handled. Currently, opening an editor subscribes a client's ActionCable WebSocket to a shared stream (e.g., `Turbo::StreamsChannel` with `signed_stream_name` for `[leaf, :being_edited]`). This subscription is based on the initial access the user had. The server broadcasts updates to this shared stream, and everyone subscribed receives them, regardless of their current editing rights. Even if a user is later removed, their existing subscription remains active because the subscription only validates the HMAC signature but doesn't check authorization on subscribe.

2.  **Proposed Solution: Per-User/Custom Streams**: The solution is to move to a per-user, or more correctly, per-editor channel/stream. Instead of broadcasting to a shared stream, each editor should subscribe to a stream specific to their user (`[leaf, :being_edited, current_user]` or a custom channel).

    *   This per-user approach allows for fine-grained control:
        *   When a user opens the editor, they subscribe to their own stream.
        *   When a user is removed, broadcasts are stopped to their stream (because the server checks if the user *is* an editor).
        *   The channel can check the authorization (`leaf.book.editable?(user: current_user)`) on subscription/re-subscription and reject it if access is revoked.
        *   This *also* covers the edge case where someone had an old signed stream and tried to use it!
        *   A custom channel (e.g. `BeingEditedChannel`) with authorization checks is strictly better!

    *   This per-user approach ensures that only *currently* authorized editors receive the "being edited" updates. When User Y saves, the broadcast would *only* go to `[leaf, :being_edited, User Y]` and any other editors, never User X who was removed.

    *   If a user is re-added, their new session would allow them to re-subscribe and receive the presence payload.

    *   If a user has an old tab open after re-added, the existing subscription is rejected by the custom channel `subscribed` check!

3.  **Testing and Edge Cases**: Thorough testing is crucial. I've considered several scenarios:

    *   **Scenario 1: Removal While Open:** A collaborator with editor access opens a page and another user removes them. The system needs to ensure that the removed user *doesn't* receive any further broadcasts. A system test or browser test with ActionCable is necessary.

    *   **Scenario 2: Reconnection After Removal:** A removed user tries to reconnect using the old subscription details. The custom channel needs to reject this subscription.

    *   **Scenario 3: Disconnection**: Disconnecting a user *should not* be necessary. If using a per-user stream, the lack of broadcasts to the old stream solves the problem. A test needs to verify that `ActionCable.server.remote_connections.where(current_user: user).disconnect` is *not* necessary.
        *   Moreover, disconnects should be avoided to avoid dropping other tabs for the same user.

    *   **Administrator Access**: It's essential to account for administrators. Administrators may not have an *Access* record to a book but can still edit if they are an active administrator. So, the stream scope must include admins by checking `book.editable?(user: user)` and `user.active?` or the equivalent, or `user.administrator?`.

4.  **Implementation Details & `broadcast_render_later_to`**:

    *   Current code uses `Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_render_later_to`. This broadcasts to the channel.

    *   The channel broadcasts the same partial multiple times (i.e. to each editor).

    *   We can avoid broadcasting to `Current.user` if necessary, but we need to check if existing tests or functionality depend on that broadcast, and whether excluding the current user avoids an unintended consequence.

module Authentication
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern
  include SessionLookup

  included do
    before_action :require_authentication
    helper_method :signed_in?

    protect_from_forgery with: :exception, unless: -> { authenticated_by.bot_key? }
  end

  class_methods do
    def require_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      allow_unauthenticated_access **options
      before_action :redirect_signed_in_user_to_root, **options
    end

    def allow_unauthenticated_access(**options)
      skip_before_action :require_authentication, **options
      before_action :restore_authentication, **options
    end
  end

  private
    def signed_in?
      Current.user.present?
    end

    def require_authentication
      restore_authentication || request_authentication
    end

    def restore_authentication
      if session = find_session_by_cookie
        resume_session session
      end
    end

    def request_authentication
      session[:return_to_after_authenticating] = request.url
      redirect_to new_session_url
    end

    def redirect_signed_in_user_to_root
      redirect_to root_url if signed_in?
    end

    def start_new_session_for(user)
      user.sessions.start!(user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip).tap do |session|
        authenticated_as session
      end
    end

    def resume_session(session)
      session.resume user_agent: request.user_agent, ip_address: request.remote_ip
      authenticated_as session
    end

    def terminate_current_session
      Current.session&.destroy!
      reset_session
      remove_authentication_cookie
    end

    def authenticated_as(session)
      Current.session = session
      set_authenticated_by(:session)
      set_authentication_cookie(session)
    end

    def post_authenticating_url
      session.delete(:return_to_after_authenticating) || root_url
    end

    def set_authentication_cookie(session)
      cookies.signed.permanent[:session_token] = { value: session.token, httponly: true, same_site: :lax }
    end

    def remove_authentication_cookie
      cookies.delete(:session_token)
    end

    def set_authenticated_by(method)
      @authenticated_by = method.to_s.inquiry
    end

    def authenticated_by
      @authenticated_by ||= "".inquiry
    end
end

messages.thinking:
**Design Deep Dive: Being Edited Indicator**

Alright, let's dissect this indicator setup meticulously, ensuring robustness. My goal is to revamp the "being edited" feature and nail down every edge case.

First, I need to revisit the existing implementation. The indicator itself lives in `app/views/leaves/_being_edited_indicator.html.erb`, neatly rendered within the `edit.html.erb` page.  This is where the Turbo Streams magic starts with `turbo_stream_from`. The broadcast originates from the `LeafablesController` within the `update` action. The `broadcast_being_edited_indicator` method uses `Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_render_later_to`, which, as a side note, I'm already mentally noting to potentially improve for more control. The broadcast generates a stream containing the user who is editing.

Now, it's time to refine this.  The core idea is to move away from a shared stream and explore a dedicated channel. Let's start by brainstorming a channel name, perhaps `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel` or a simplified `BeingEditedChannel`. I need to consult the `app/channels/` directory to stick with conventions.

Okay, let's explore. I'll need to understand how `turbo_stream_from` functions with a custom channel. I see that  `turbo_stream_from` uses `<turbo-cable-stream-source>` under the hood. The `channel` attribute, if provided, is used, and the signed stream name is passed too.  I'm now contemplating two primary approaches.

**Option A:** In `_being_edited_indicator.html.erb`, use `<%= turbo_stream_from leaf, :being_edited, channel: BeingEditedChannel %>`. Then, in `BeingEditedChannel`, parse the `signed_stream_name` for `leaf` using  `GlobalID::Locator.locate` and check the stream against the current user's permissions and leaf state. Then, append the current user to the stream.

**Option B:** In `_being_edited_indicator.html.erb`, use `<%= turbo_stream_from leaf, :being_edited, Current.user, channel: BeingEditedChannel %>`. This seems cleaner. The `signed_stream_name` would directly contain the leaf, the "being_edited" suffix, and the current user. In `BeingEditedChannel`, I would check if `user == current_user` and verify permissions, and only then stream.

With option B,  the stream name is constructed exactly as the Turbo Streams documentation specifies, which ensures the verification method is consistent with how the signed name is generated.  The added benefit is that the `signed_stream_name` must always be constructed by the app with the current user. This prevents a potential security vulnerability where an attacker could construct their own signed stream name with their user ID to trick the app.  If anyone tried to pass someone else's stream name, it would be rejected because `user == current_user` check would fail!

This looks very promising. Option B simplifies both the view and the channel logic, while providing strong security. I can now be confident this design is both robust and secure.

messages.thinking:
**Deep Dive into "Being Edited" Broadcasts**

Okay, so initially I was thinking, "Great, `GlobalID::Locator.locate(gid_param)` works right out of the box!" But hold on, let's not get complacent. My mind immediately went into overdrive, considering every possible edge case, every tiny hiccup that could arise. Let's make sure this is solid.

The first edge case that jumped out involved collaborators and their changing access. What if someone gets removed, then added back, or if a browser tries to reconnect a removed user? Let's break it down:

*   **Scenario:** Collaborator A is editing. They get removed from the book. Collaborator B saves.
    *   Previously, the stream was a single stream for the leaf, so both would get the broadcast.
    *   Now, with per-user streams, Collaborator A is listening on their own stream, and Collaborator B's save ONLY broadcasts to the *active* editors of the book.
    *   The crucial thing is, if A is no longer an editor, there's *no* broadcast sent to their stream. Zero payload!
    *   This is PERFECT because the problem is solved! A can't receive it because they are not an editor.

*   **Reconnect Scenario:** What if A's browser tries to reconnect after being removed?
    *   The `BeingEditedChannel#subscribed` method kicks in and does these checks:
        *   `leaf.is_a?(Leaf) && leaf.active? && current_user.active? && leaf.book.editable?(user: current_user)`
    *   Thank goodness for `leaf.active?` — if the leaf is trashed, it can't be edited!
    *   If A is not an editor (or is deactivated, or the leaf is trashed), the `subscribed` method *rejects* the subscription.

Next, I thought about whether `Current.user` (the person *saving*) should receive their own broadcast. Should we exclude them? Let's see what's happening in the code:

*   The view (`leaves/_being_edited_by.turbo_stream.erb`) appends a `turbo_stream` to display the "being edited" indicator. It includes a `data` attribute (`hide_from_user_id: user.id`).
*   The `application_helper.rb` has this method: `hide_from_user_style_tag`.
*   Let's see what this is all about:
    *   The `hide_from_user_id` attribute was there *because* the old broadcast went to a single stream. The user who saved was getting their own broadcast.
    *   Now, if we exclude `Current.user` from the broadcast (`editors.where.not(id: Current.user.id)`), it means a *slightly* less efficient broadcast, but the correct outcome. The person saving doesn't need to be told they are saving.
    *   And it's a good thing, because `hide_from_user_id` was *already* hiding the indicator from `Current.user` anyway! They don't need to see it, and it saves on wasted WebSocket traffic.

**Final Thoughts:** After a LOT of deliberation, I've concluded that excluding the `Current.user` from the broadcast is the way to go. It aligns perfectly with the intended functionality (showing who is *currently* editing to *other* editors), improves efficiency, and reduces unnecessary data transfer. messages.thinking:
**Refining the "Being Edited" Broadcast Logic**

Okay, so I've been thinking about this "being edited" indicator, and I think I've got a solid optimization in mind. The current setup, keeping things like `hide_from_user_id` and `hide_from_user_style_tag`, doesn't introduce any harm. Excluding `Current.user` in the `broadcast_being_edited_indicator` method is crucial to avoid unnecessary broadcasts to the person who's saving. After all, they don't need to see the "being edited" indicator for themselves. This also prevents an unneeded WebSocket message from being sent if it's the only editor.

However, I'm now honing in on an edge case with `Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_render_later_to` vs rendering once and broadcasting.  Let's look at the implementation. Currently, we're using `broadcast_render_later_to`, which, uses ActiveJob for async processing. My initial thought was to iterate through the editors, excluding the current user.

My concern is the underlying mechanics of `broadcast_render_later_to`. Specifically, how it handles the job queue.  If a user is removed from a book *after* the job is enqueued but *before* it executes, that broadcast could be sent to a user who no longer has access. The `Turbo::Streams::BroadcastJob` only has the stream name (a string), it doesn't know to re-check if the editor still has access.

My solution: I'm leaning toward a custom job (e.g., `BeingEditedBroadcastJob`).  This custom job would check at execution time whether the leaf is active and the user is still an editor. This single job would render the partial *once*, and then broadcast to the current editors.

This custom job would:

1.  Run asynchronously via ActiveJob (same as `broadcast_render_later_to`).
2.  Check `@leaf.active?` and `user.active?` and queries `@leaf.book.editors.where.not(id: user.id)` AT EXECUTION TIME!
3.  Render the partial ONCE and store the content!
4.  For each *current* editor, call `ActionCable.server.broadcast(stream_name, content)` (or `BeingEditedChannel.broadcast_stream_to(leaf, :being_edited, editor, content: content)` or `BeingEditedChannel.broadcast_to(...)`)!
5.  Check authorization before the broadcast.

This approach offers multiple advantages:

*   Only one job is enqueued per save, rather than N.
*   Only one template render happens per save, rather than N.
*   Authorization is checked right before the actual broadcast.

And to be certain, I want to confirm whether a custom `ApplicationJob` plays nicely with Rails testing tools like `assert_enqueued_with` and `perform_enqueued_jobs`. The good news is, they work perfectly fine.  `perform_enqueued_jobs` handles all enqueued ActiveJob jobs, and `assert_turbo_stream_broadcasts` in `turbo-rails` is compatible as well!  I'm also inspecting `turbo-rails` test helpers to confirm it.

      # In addition to a String, the helper also accepts an Object or Array to
      # determine the name of the channel the elements are broadcast to:
      #
      #     message = Message.find(1)
      #
      #     replace, remove = capture_turbo_stream_broadcasts message do
      #       message.broadcast_replace
      #       message.broadcast_remove
      #     end
      #
      #     assert_equal "replace", replace["action"]
      #     assert_equal "replace", remove["action"]
      #
      def capture_turbo_stream_broadcasts(stream_name_or_object, &block)
        block&.call

        stream_name = stream_name_from(stream_name_or_object)
        payloads = broadcasts(stream_name)

        payloads.flat_map do |payload|
          html = ActiveSupport::JSON.decode(payload)
          document = Nokogiri::HTML5.parse(html)

          document.at("body").element_children
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

The prompt said, specifically, the payload must not go out on a channel a removed collaborator can still be listening on.

My thoughts then turned to other edge cases and whether a `disconnect` call (e.g. `remote_connections.disconnect`) would be needed. **My Analysis of the "Being Edited" Indicator Implementation**

Okay, here's what I've got after this deep dive: the original problem was `GlobalID::Locator.locate` returning `nil`, but that doesn't seem to be an issue anymore. Now, I've got a comprehensive understanding of how the broadcasting of "being edited" indicators *should* work.

First, I examined the `LeafablesController` and its `broadcast_being_edited_indicator` method. We have two main approaches to broadcasting: per-editor with `Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_render_later_to`, or via a dedicated job like `Leaves::BeingEditedBroadcastJob`. After a careful comparison, the dedicated job seems far superior.

Using a job, we can centralize the logic, ensure that we only render the partial *once*, and perform crucial checks before broadcasting. It seems like the critical piece is to check that the editor is still active, that the leaf is still valid, and that the editor still has permission to edit *at the time the job executes*, not when it's *enqueued*. This is a huge win. We're preventing a lot of potential stale broadcast issues. This also ensures that we only broadcast to active editors *at the moment of the broadcast*, not at the moment of the save.

The job itself checks if the editor *and* leaf are still active and that the editor still has access to the book, and queries the current list of editors. This eliminates race conditions where someone might be removed from a book after the job has been queued but before it runs. Also, we're making sure we only render the partial *once*, instead of rendering it repeatedly for each editor. The use of `ApplicationController.render` (or `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel.render_format`) and then passing the rendered content to `broadcast_stream_to` makes it very clean and efficient, especially when there are no editors at all.

I've confirmed that the broadcasting mechanism, leveraging `ActionCable.server.broadcast` and Turbo Streams, works perfectly: it directly delivers the `<turbo-stream>` HTML. And the corresponding tests with `assert_turbo_stream_broadcasts` work exactly as expected.

I also considered a variety of edge cases that could break the implementation. These included collaborator removal, downgrading of permissions, deactivation, and administrator demotion. In all these cases, with the job approach, the indicator broadcast *correctly* stops for the user who no longer has edit access. We don't have to worry about old subscriptions receiving stale data. I also checked potential attack vectors, like someone trying to subscribe with an old stream name or a reader trying to get into an editor's channel. Those cases are handled correctly.

We're also covered when a removed collaborator is *re-added*, either as a reader or an editor. We also considered the case when someone keeps a tab open, but is then removed from a book. Again, the system *correctly* doesn't broadcast the indicator. I've even checked how Action Cable's `TestCase` works in that context. The system is resilient to someone trying to use `ActionCable::Channel::TestCase` to subscribe with an old stream. It won't work, and that's good.

I checked what happens with `BooksController#edit`/`BooksController#update`/Access Model when a collaborator is removed, as well as checking `Current.user` in `Turbo::StreamsChannel`. I've confirmed that the use of `turbo_stream_from` helper is generating the correct `<turbo-cable-stream-source>` tag, and the subscription flow is also working as expected. Okay, so the fixtures are loaded inside `bin/rails test`, which is good to know. We can build out comprehensive tests—integration and channel tests—right in `test/`, or run a standalone test using `bin/rails test`. Before diving in, let's carefully design the code changes to make sure everything's crystal clear.

First, focusing on `app/models/book/accessable.rb`, the plan is to add an `editors` method. This method needs to return the users who can currently edit a book. I'll need to carefully verify how `Book#editors` behaves in different scenarios: when the book has `everyone_access: true` versus `false`; when users are active or inactive; and when users have `reader`, `editor`, or `administrator` roles. I must remember that `User.active` appears on both sides of the `.or(...)`, so the active status is guaranteed.

Next, the `app/channels/leaves/being_edited_channel.rb` needs some design adjustments.  We're looking at allowing a user to subscribe if they can be verified. Let's make sure the `stream_name` is validated correctly. Checking for extra colons in `stream_name` using `split(":", 3)` is the better way. And it's good to ensure that `leaf.to_gid_param` or `user.to_gid_param` *never* contain colons. We can check that the size of the array is equal to three and the second element equals "being_edited". We have full control!

Then, the `app/jobs/leaves/being_edited_broadcast_job.rb` needs a detailed review. I have to think about what happens if `leaf` is trashed *after* save, if `editor` is deactivated or removed *before* job execution, and if a recipient changes status before the job runs. The code's checks seem robust: `leaf.active?`, `editor.active? && leaf.book.editable?(user: editor)`, and the database query to get editors all handle these cases.  Also, if the recipient list is empty, we simply skip the broadcasting altogether. Now, instead of rendering a partial for each recipient, we render it *once* and call the broadcasting function for each authorized person.

Moving on, the `app/controllers/leafables_controller.rb` needs to be updated. Replacing the direct `Turbo::StreamsChannel.broadcast_render_later_to` call with a `Leaves::BeingEditedBroadcastJob.perform_later` invocation seems right, making it more efficient with a job.

In `app/views/leaves/_being_edited_indicator.html.erb`, we need to change `turbo_stream_from` to pass the user and the channel.

Now, a critical step: *Double-checking the logic*. Is there any scenario where deactivating a user or updating a book's access rights could leave a connection or session open, creating inconsistencies? No. If a user is removed, downgraded, or deactivated, the system ensures that their streams are closed or the broadcast is rejected based on the `active?` check or permissions check in the channel.

Finally, even more detail: What if a user is *removed* from the book, and then *re-added* as an editor while they still have an edit tab open? That scenario is handled correctly. At the time a user *is* an editor, the system will function, ensuring that the broadcast *is* authorized if the user has been re-added.

Remember to look at where tests live in the repo, looking in `test/controllers/leafables_controller_test.rb`, `test/channels/`, `test/models/book/accessable_test.rb`, and `test/jobs/` to inform the tests needed.

4.  **The Failure:** And here's the kicker – right now, the stream `kevin` is subscribed to *receives* a broadcast that it shouldn't, containing `"David"` which is the culprit.

require "test_helper"

class BeingEditedReproTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  include ActiveJob::TestHelper
  include ActionCable::TestHelper

  test "removed collaborator still receives being edited payload on subscribed stream" do
    leaf = leaves(:welcome_page)
    book = books(:handbook)

    # 1. Kevin opens the page editor while he has editor access
    sign_in :kevin
    get edit_book_page_path(book, leaf)
    assert_response :success

    stream_source = css_select("turbo-cable-stream-source").first
    assert stream_source, "Expected turbo-cable-stream-source element"
    signed_stream_name = stream_source["signed-stream-name"]
    stream_name = Turbo::StreamsChannel.verified_stream_name(signed_stream_name)

    # 2. Kevin is removed from the book
    book.update_access(editors: [ users(:david).id, users(:jason).id ], readers: [])
    assert_not book.accessable?(user: users(:kevin))
    assert_not book.editable?(user: users(:kevin))

    # 3. David saves the page
    sign_in :david
    perform_enqueued_jobs do
      patch book_page_path(book, leaf), params: { page: { body: "Updated body" } }
      assert_response :no_content
    end

    # 4. Assert no broadcast went to the stream Kevin subscribed to
    assert_no_broadcasts stream_name
  end
end

class Leaves::BeingEditedChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  extend Turbo::Streams::Broadcasts, Turbo::Streams::StreamName
  include Turbo::Streams::StreamName::ClassMethods

  def subscribed
    if (stream_name = verified_stream_name_from_params).present? && subscription_allowed?(stream_name)
      stream_from stream_name
    else
      reject
    end
  end

  private
    def subscription_allowed?(stream_name)
      parts = stream_name.split(":")
      return false unless parts.size == 3 && parts[1] == "being_edited"

      leaf = GlobalID::Locator.locate(parts[0])
      user = GlobalID::Locator.locate(parts[2])

      leaf.is_a?(Leaf) && leaf.active? &&
        user.present? && user == current_user && current_user.active? &&
        leaf.book.editable?(user: current_user)
    end
end

class Leaves::BeingEditedBroadcastJob < ApplicationJob
  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  def perform(leaf, editor)
    return unless leaf.active? && editor.active? && leaf.book.editable?(user: editor)

    recipients = leaf.book.editors.where.not(id: editor.id).to_a
    return if recipients.empty?

    content = ApplicationController.render(
      formats: [ :turbo_stream ],
      partial: "leaves/being_edited_by",
      locals: { leaf: leaf, user: editor }
    )

    recipients.each do |recipient|
      Leaves::BeingEditedChannel.broadcast_stream_to leaf, :being_edited, recipient, content: content
    end
  end
end
EOF

*   **Administrator Access:** An administrator, even without an explicit `Access` record, should be able to subscribe. We'll make sure this is confirmed.
*   **Access Denied:** Now, the important part: a reader (like `jz`) should be *rejected*. Also, a collaborator without book access (e.g. `kevin` on `manual`) must be blocked.
*   **Revoked Access:** We'll test what happens if a collaborator is removed from the book *after* they received a `signed_stream_name` - subscription must fail.
*   **Unauthorized Use:** Testing scenarios where someone tries to subscribe with another user's `signed_stream_name` is crucial, as well as handling deactivated users and trashed leaves, all of these should result in a rejection.
*   **Invalid Data:** The channel needs to reject any subscription attempt with an invalid, missing, or tampered `signed_stream_name`. Also, the correct streamable type is a requirement, so anything outside of `[leaf, :being_edited, user]` should be rejected.

Next, I'll move on to `Book#editors` in `test/models/book/accessable_test.rb`. This is where I want to ensure that it correctly returns active editors and administrators, excluding readers, removed users, and deactivated users. The filter needs to be solid.

Finally, I'll tackle the controller tests, likely in `test/controllers/leafables_controller_test.rb` or `test/controllers/pages_controller_test.rb`. These tests are about the *real-world* usage:

*   **Editor Page Load:** When an editor, say `kevin`, visits the edit page, the page *should* subscribe to `Leaves::BeingEditedChannel` with a properly scoped stream.
*   **Broadcasts on Save:** Now, the crux of the feature. When another editor, such as `david`, saves the page, here's what must happen:
    *   Active editors *other than* `david` should receive a turbo-stream broadcast containing `"David"`. This confirms the active editing broadcast is working.
    *   `david` (the saving editor) should *not* receive a broadcast of their own save.
    *   Readers should *not* receive any broadcast.
    *   And, crucially, the *old* shared stream `[leaf, :being_edited]` should NOT be receiving broadcasts.
*   **Revoked Mid-Session:** This is the critical edge case. What happens if `kevin` is removed from the book (or downgraded, or deactivated) *while* they still have the edit page open, and *then* `david` saves? We need to verify that `kevin` does *not* receive *any* broadcasts! Remaining active editors, like `jason`, must STILL receive broadcasts.
*   **Job Race Condition:** If `kevin` is removed *after* the broadcast job has been enqueued (but before it executes), they should *still* not receive broadcasts! This is to ensure that jobs are checking permissions or that we can cancel the broadcasts.

class Leaves::BeingEditedChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  extend Turbo::Streams::Broadcasts, Turbo::Streams::StreamName
  include Turbo::Streams::StreamName::ClassMethods

  def subscribed
    if (stream_name = verified_stream_name_from_params).present? && subscription_allowed?(stream_name)
      stream_from stream_name
    else
      reject
    end
  end

  private
    def subscription_allowed?(stream_name)
      parts = stream_name.split(":")
      return false unless parts.size == 3 && parts[1] == "being_edited"

      leaf = GlobalID::Locator.locate(parts[0])
      user = GlobalID::Locator.locate(parts[2])

      leaf.is_a?(Leaf) && leaf.active? &&
        user.present? && user == current_user && current_user.active? &&
        leaf.book.editable?(user: current_user)
    end
end
=== app/jobs/leaves/being_edited_broadcast_job.rb ===
class Leaves::BeingEditedBroadcastJob < ApplicationJob
  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  def perform(leaf, editor)
    return unless leaf.active? && editor.active? && leaf.book.editable?(user: editor)

    recipients = leaf.book.editors.where.not(id: editor.id).to_a
    return if recipients.empty?

    content = ApplicationController.render(
      formats: [ :turbo_stream ],
      partial: "leaves/being_edited_by",
      locals: { leaf: leaf, user: editor }
    )

    recipients.each do |recipient|
      Leaves::BeingEditedChannel.broadcast_stream_to leaf, :being_edited, recipient, content: content
    end
  end
end

=== app/channels/leaves/being_edited_channel.rb ===
class Leaves::BeingEditedChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  extend Turbo::Streams::Broadcasts, Turbo::Streams::StreamName
  include Turbo::Streams::StreamName::ClassMethods

  def subscribed
    if (stream_name = verified_stream_name_from_params).present? && subscription_allowed?(stream_name)
      stream_from stream_name
    else
      reject
    end
  end

  private
    def subscription_allowed?(stream_name)
      parts = stream_name.split(":")
      return false unless parts.size == 3 && parts[1] == "being_edited"

      leaf = GlobalID::Locator.locate(parts[0])
      user = GlobalID::Locator.locate(parts[2])

      leaf.is_a?(Leaf) && leaf.active? &&
        user.present? && user == current_user && current_user.active? &&
        leaf.book.editable?(user: current_user)
    end
end
=== app/jobs/leaves/being_edited_broadcast_job.rb ===
class Leaves::BeingEditedBroadcastJob < ApplicationJob
  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  def perform(leaf, editor)
    return unless leaf.active? && editor.active? && leaf.book.editable?(user: editor)

    recipients = leaf.book.editors.where.not(id: editor.id).to_a
    return if recipients.empty?

    content = ApplicationController.render(
      formats: [ :turbo_stream ],
      partial: "leaves/being_edited_by",
      locals: { leaf: leaf, user: editor }
    )

    recipients.each do |recipient|
      Leaves::BeingEditedChannel.broadcast_stream_to leaf, :being_edited, recipient, content: content
    end
  end
end

require "test_helper"

module Leaves
  class BeingEditedChannelTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase
    test "subscribes editor to user-scoped being edited stream" do
      stub_connection current_user: users(:kevin)

      subscribe signed_stream_name: signed_stream_name_for(leaves(:welcome_page), users(:kevin))

      assert subscription.confirmed?
      assert_has_stream Turbo::StreamsChannel.send(:stream_name_from, [ leaves(:welcome_page), :being_edited, users(:kevin) ])
    end

    test "subscribes administrator without explicit access record" do
      books(:manual).update!(published: true)
      books(:manual).accesses.where(user: users(:david)).delete_all
      leaf = books(:manual).press Page.new(body: "Hello"), title: "Admin Page"

      stub_connection current_user: users(:david)

      subscribe signed_stream_name: signed_stream_name_for(leaf, users(:david))

      assert subscription.confirmed?
    end

    test "rejects reader" do
      stub_connection current_user: users(:jz)

      subscribe signed_stream_name: signed_stream_name_for(leaves(:welcome_page), users(:jz))

      assert subscription.rejected?
    end

    test "rejects user without access to book" do
      leaf = books(:manual).press Page.new(body: "Hello"), title: "Manual Page"
      stub_connection current_user: users(:kevin)

      subscribe signed_stream_name: signed_stream_name_for(leaf, users(:kevin))

      assert subscription.rejected?
    end

    test "rejects previously authorized collaborator whose access was removed" do
      signed_name = signed_stream_name_for(leaves(:welcome_page), users(:kevin))
      books(:handbook).update!(everyone_access: false)
      books(:handbook).update_access(editors: [ users(:david).id ], readers: [])

      stub_connection current_user: users(:kevin)

      subscribe signed_stream_name: signed_name

      assert subscription.rejected?
    end

    test "rejects subscribing to another user's stream" do
      stub_connection current_user: users(:kevin)

      subscribe signed_stream_name: signed_stream_name_for(leaves(:welcome_page), users(:david))

      assert subscription.rejected?
    end

    test "rejects deactivated user" do
      users(:kevin).deactivate
      stub_connection current_user: users(:kevin)

      subscribe signed_stream_name: signed_stream_name_for(leaves(:welcome_page), users(:kevin))

      assert subscription.rejected?
    end

    test "rejects trashed leaf" do
      leaves(:welcome_page).trashed!
      stub_connection current_user: users(:kevin)

      subscribe signed_stream_name: signed_stream_name_for(leaves(:welcome_page), users(:kevin))

      assert subscription.rejected?
    end

    test "rejects missing or invalid signed stream name" do
      stub_connection current_user: users(:kevin)

      subscribe signed_stream_name: "tampered"
      assert subscription.rejected?

      subscribe signed_stream_name: Turbo::StreamsChannel.signed_stream_name([ leaves(:welcome_page), :being_edited ])
      assert subscription.rejected?

      subscribe signed_stream_name: Turbo::StreamsChannel.signed_stream_name([ books(:handbook), :being_edited, users(:kevin) ])
      assert subscription.rejected?
    end

    private
      def signed_stream_name_for(leaf, user)
        Turbo::StreamsChannel.signed_stream_name([ leaf, :being_edited, user ])
      end
  end
